kinds.task: Runs to completion; show its output and exit code.
kinds.service: Runs until stopped (SIGINT); has a ready signal where one exists.
kinds.stream: Prints continuously until stopped; nothing else depends on it.
kinds.gui: Opens a native window; runs until the window or the process is closed.
kinds.interactive: Needs keyboard input in its own terminal (PTY).
kinds.link: Something to open, not a process.

ros.label: ROS env
ros.description: Inside the platform's ROS 2 environment: Pixi env activated, workspace overlay sourced, ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42, working dir ros2_ws. Pixi task names (build, fmt) also work here.

host.label: Host
host.description: A plain shell on the host machine at the repo root, never inside a container.

host-sudo.label: Host + sudo
host-sudo.description: Host shell at the repo root; prompts for the sudo password, so run it in a terminal (PTY) the user can type into.

link.label: Link
link.description: Not a process: a URL, file or app to open.

platforms.x86-native: x86-64 Linux with the workspace built natively in ros2_ws/.pixi/envs/default (this laptop). tooling/host-ros2 strips a system /opt/ros install from the environment first.
platforms.x86-docker: x86-64 Linux + NVIDIA running the billee-desktop image (make setup x86).
platforms.mac: Apple-Silicon Mac running the billee-mac-cpu image. Headless: no RViz window, gamepad, vcan0 or DDS to other machines.
platforms.linux-aarch64: ARM64 Linux, native Pixi env, no container.
platforms.l4t: The Jetson rover, rover-ros2 image. Headless.

needs.display: An X/Wayland display for a window (RViz, Gazebo, rqt). Headless machines put xvfb-run -a in front of sim launches.
needs.vcan0: The virtual CAN interface on the host: run can.vcan-up first (sudo).
needs.can0: A real CAN interface: the Jetson's mttcan or a USB-CAN adapter, brought up with can.up.
needs.docker: Docker reachable without sudo (docker info works).
needs.rover: The physical rover. Wheels will turn: put it on blocks first.
needs.terminal: Reads keys from its own terminal: the launcher must give it an interactive PTY.
needs.drivetrain: A running drivetrain item (any of the 'drivetrain' group).

resources.drivetrain: Only one at a time. Each starts /controller_manager, /diff_drive_controller and /robot_state_publisher; two would publish conflicting odometry and TF.
resources.port-8765: foxglove_bridge's WebSocket port. One bridge per machine; a second one fails to bind.
resources.gamepad-nodes: joy_node + joy_tank_drive. The sim always starts a pair (joy_control:=false is ignored), teleop.launch.py and ground_station.launch.py start another. Two pairs publish duplicate commands, and an idle pad publishes zeros at 20 Hz.
resources.cmd-vel: /diff_drive_controller/cmd_vel_unstamped. Every publisher here commands the wheels; the controller obeys the last message received.

items.label: Mock drivetrain
items.cmd: ros2 launch chassis_bringup rover.launch.py mode:=real can_interface:=mock
items.verified: controllers active in under 1 s; odom and joint_states at 30 Hz; bridge on :8765
items.notes: The real (non-Gazebo) stack with a software loopback in the ODESC plugin. No CAN, motors, Gazebo or GPU. Fastest loop. Wall-clock time (use_sim_time:=false for separate viewers). Starts no teleop.

items.label: Gazebo simulation
items.notes: Gazebo Fortress, empty world, Foxglove bridge always on. Also starts gamepad teleop (it can't be turned off). Sim time: viewers need use_sim_time:=true. Opens a Gazebo window; headless machines prefix xvfb-run -a (not installed on this laptop, which also has no NVIDIA driver, so Gazebo renders on the CPU).

items.label: Virtual CAN bench
items.cmd: ros2 launch chassis_bringup rover.launch.py mode:=real can_interface:=vcan0
items.notes: The real ODESC driver talking to a virtual bus. Pair with addons.emulator for feedback, and can.dump to watch frames (six 0x07 on activate, 0x0D per command).

items.label: Real drivetrain
items.notes: 6× ODESC V4.2 + NEO over can0 at 500 kbit/s. Motion only with a command stream; wheels stop 0.25 s after the last command. First runs on blocks.

items.label: Hardware backend (no bridge)
items.notes: What rover.launch.py mode:=real wraps, without forcing the bridge on. Writes a temp controllers.yaml with use_sim_time: false.

items.label: ODESC vCAN emulator
items.verified: ros2 run: 'No executable found'. The script is committed without the executable bit (git mode 100644) and --symlink-install links to it, so odesc_shadow:=true hits 'Permission denied' too. python3 <path> works.
items.notes: Answers as nodes 0–5 with 0x09 encoder frames at 100 Hz. Fix in the repo: git update-index --chmod=+x ros2_ws/src/odesc/scripts/odesc_vcan_emulator.py.

items.label: Restart the ros2 CLI daemon
items.cmd: ros2 daemon stop; ros2 daemon start
items.notes: Fixes ros2 topic/node list showing things that no longer exist, and 'Could not determine the type for the passed topic'. The daemon is shared per ROS_DOMAIN_ID, so one started with different settings (e.g. ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1) gives stale answers. Echo items here pass the message type so they don't need it.

items.label: Start the long-lived ROS container
items.notes: Launcher pattern: start this first, then every ros item joins it via docker exec. The first desktop-ros2 run owns the container (--rm), so if a sim is the first process, stopping the sim kills everything else in that container.
